propositions: Per-candidate overlap judgments currently require 2N calls (one per candidate per ordering), re-sending the 846-token system prefix on every call; batching N candidates into one user message per ordering reduces this to 2*ceil(N/batch) calls, saving ~8,460 tokens on N=6 by eliminating ten prefix copies

The batched system prefix (base 423 + hoisted query digest 306-453 + batch protocol section +436) reaches 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token caching floor and enabling cache_write/read; the original per-pair approach maxes out at 873 tokens below the floor with cache_write=0

Batching introduces cross-contamination risk; verdict parity testing on one query and six candidates shows 5/5 runs with identical surfaced findings and 6/12 ordered pairs with shifted relation labels (mostly conservative, moving away from false positives), with a synthetic duplicate injected as positive control recovered at full confidence in both orderings

Measured on real anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6 calls: pre-8415 baseline 17,558 input tokens and 12 calls; post-batching 9,116 input tokens and 2 calls (−48.1%), with cache_write 1,331 then cache_read 1,331 on the second call

Batched build must yield strictly fewer calls than 2N candidates, each candidate receives exactly one verdict matched by label not position, a raising runner or malformed response yields empty verdict list with no exception escape, and total input tokens must stay below 16,040 (the pre-8415 baseline)

All new tests mutation-checked in both directions: call-count reduction, batch-per-ordering slot preservation, label-based demultiplexing, duplicate-entry guard, and fail-safe error handling each killed by specific mutations and pass on restored tree
